I did all this on Ubuntu 16.04, it probably won't work with Cygwin/MinGW but I haven't tested it. This "guide" assumes you have at least a little bit of experience with GNU/Linux systems. Please note that I PROBABLY forgot a few things here and there, but I believe I got all the big important ones.

INSTALLING OPENCL HEADERS

sudo apt-get install ocl-icd-opencl-dev opencl-headers

INSTALLING RADEONTOP Radeontop just allows you to monitor your GPU usage so you can make sure it's actually being used.

cd ~/
git clone https://github.com/clbr/radeontop
sudo make
sudo make install

INSTALLING AMDGPU-PRO DRIVERS Go to support.amd.com and download the latest driver for your card, extract it somewhere and then open a terminal there

./amdgpu-pro-install -y
sudo reboot

After you reboot, go back to the same location and run

./amdgpu-pro-install -compute -y

INSTALLING PYTHON 3.6.4 download Python 3.6.4 source here

extract it somewhere

./configure
sudo make
sudo make install

INSTALL PIP3.6

~~~ sudo apt-get install python3-pip pip install --upgrade pip ~~~ (this might have to be pip3.6 install --upgrade pip3.6?)

INSTALLING GIT

sudo apt-get install git

CLONING FACESWAP

cd ~/
git clone https://github.com/deepfakes/faceswap

INSTALLING VIRTUALENV AND CREATING A PYTHON VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT

pip3.6 install virtualenv
cd ~/faceswap
virtualenv faceswap_env/

CONFIGURING FACESWAP

pip3.6 install -r requirements-gpu.txt
pip3.6 uninstall tensorflow
pip3.6 uninstall keras

Now come the hard parts. BUILDING BAZEL FROM SOURCE UPDATE you may not have to build bazel from source after all? try this first and then only build from source if that doesn't work.

To build from source: https://docs.bazel.build/versions/master/install-compile-source.html

INSTALLING COMPUTECPP download computecpp from https://www.codeplay.com/products/computesuite/computecpp add the following to the end of your ~/.bashrc file:

export TF_NEED_OPENCL=1
export HOST_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-4.8
export HOST_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/gcc-4.8
export COMPUTECPP_TOOLKIT_PATH=/usr/local/computecpp
export COMPUTE=:0

Now extract the contents of the archive you downloaded from Codeplay to

/usr/local/computecpp

INTSTALL CLINFO

sudo apt-get install clinfo

Now run clinfo and make sure your GPU is exposed to OpenCL

INSTALL CURL

sudo apt-get install curl linux-generic

BUILDING TENSORFLOW WITH OPENCL SUPPORT First, activate your virtualenv:

cd ~/faceswap/faceswap_env/bin
source activate

Now proceed:

cd ~/
git clone https://github.com/lukeiwanski/tensorflow.git
cd tensorflow
git checkout dev/amd_gpu
./configure

UPDATE Here is an updated pip wheel compiled on Ubuntu 16.04, if your CPU supports AVX, SSE4.1, and SSE4.2 instruction sets, you can just install this instead of building bazel and tensorflow yourself.

https://mega.nz/#!7QQmkToJ!s9rgaE33JkQnEwIgMxv4wFJcWqntAMtljJq59MqKpSQ

If you're not on Ubuntu 16.04, I don't know if that pip wheel will work, but it's 70MB and if it does, will let you skip the entire bazel/tensorflow installation step.

If you installed Bazel incorrect, it will now tell you. If you installed it correctly, it will say "You have Bazel [version] installed." Now it will ask you to confirm the location of your Python installation: this should be the place python is installed in inside the virtualenv, for me, that's /home/tyrannosaur/faceswap/faceswap_env/bin/python, if it's correct, just hit enter. if the last was correct, hit enter again when it asks you to confirm your Python Library path.

  • say NO to jemalloc support
  • say NO to Google Cloud support
  • say NO to Hadoop support
  • say NO to Amazon S3 support
  • say NO to XLA JIT support
  • say NO to GDR support
  • say NO to VERBS support
  • say YES to OpenCL SYCL support
  • say YES to ComputeCPP support
  • say NO to CUDA support
  • say NO to MPI support

When asked about half-types and double-types, I had to say no to half-types or else it would fail to build, but doubles worked fine. YMMV.

If everything configured correctly, you can now run the following to build a Pip wheel (Warning: this is going to take a very long time)

bazel build -c opt --config=sycl //tensorflow/tools/pip_package:build_pip_package
mkdir /tmp/tensorflow_pkg
bazel-bin/tensorflow/tools/pip_package/build_pip_package /tmp/tensorflow_pkg

If it built correctly, proceed

cd /tmp/tensorflow_pkg

Verify that your virtualenv is still running, your terminal should say (faceswap_env) before your account and hostname at the prompt.

pip3.6 install tensorflow-1.5.0rc0-cp36-cp36m-linux_x86_64.whl

If that installed correctly, proceed:

pip3.6 install keras
pip3.6 install face_recognition

Once those are installed, I think you're done. There may be some small dependencies I forgot, but they should be easy to diagnose and install. If everything worked correctly, you should be good to test: follow the instructions in ~/faceswap/USAGE.md and remember to run

sudo radeontop

to make sure your GPU is being utilized. You may also wish to run

sudo watch sensors

To make sure your GPU isn't overheating.
